In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
the combined analysis of the ADR- with the Inra-design increased the number of detected QTL by approximately 20%, and that the number of confirmed QTL was increased by approximately 50%.
a combined analysis of the ADR-design and the Inra design is a simple, efficient, and cost-effective way to increase the statistical power for QTL detection.
a combined analysis of the data from different designs is useful for QTL confirmation, but it is even more powerful for QTL detection and for the detection of new QTL.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
the JOINT-design is more powerful than the ADR- as well as than the Inra-design for QTL mapping in dairy cattle.
the joint analysis of the two designs resulted in a significant gain in power to detect QTL for all traits, and the number of QTL mapped was increased for most traits.
the experimental power of the combined analysis is increased and that the number of QTL mapped is increased, while the number of false positive QTL is not increased compared with the single designs.
The main takeaway from our work is that
a joint analysis of data sets from different granddaughter designs is a promising tool for the confirmation of previously detected QTL and the identification of novel QTL.
the power to detect QTL can be increased considerably, even if the data are collected from different granddaughter designs.
combining different granddaughter designs in one analysis can increase the power for detecting QTL.
